Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $R$ satisfying the following axioms. Axiom (A) requires a zero object and binary differential graded direct sums. Axiom (B) requires dg shift functors $[n]$, with $[0]=\mathrm{id}$ and $[n+m]=[n]\circ[m]$, and composition-compatible identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)[n]$ of dg modules. Axiom (C) requires, for every closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$, an admissible short exact sequence $y\to c(f)\to x[1]$ in $\operatorname{Comp}(\mathcal A)$ whose connecting morphism $x[1]\to y[1]$ agrees with $f[1]$. given a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{x\ar[r]^f\ar[d]_a & y\ar[d]^b\\
z\ar[r]^g & w}
$$
in $\text{Comp}(\mathcal{A})$ commuting up to homotopy. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is an admissible monomorphism, then $b$ is homotopic
to a morphism $b'$ which makes the diagram commute.
\item If $g$ is an admissible epimorphism, then $a$ is homotopic
to a morphism $a'$ which makes the diagram commute.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: A dg category satisfies the expanded axioms (A),(B),(C), and a square with arrows f,g,a,b in its degree-zero category commutes up to homotopy.
conclusions: If f is an admissible monomorphism, b can be homotopically replaced to make the square strictly commute; if g is an admissible epimorphism, a can instead be replaced so that it strictly commutes.

reason: For the admissible monomorphism case the source gives the explicit rectification b'=b−d(hπ), proving the square strictly commutes. But its dual admissible epimorphism case is explicitly omitted at line 3714; the second conclusion needs targeted proof review before a clean verdict.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor
between differential graded categories over $R$ satisfying axioms
(A), (B), and (C) such that $F(x[1]) = F(x)[1]$.
Then $F$ induces an exact functor
$K(\mathcal{A}) \to K(\mathcal{B})$ of triangulated categories.
